title: Compact variant vetting and regression signal harness for quant profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated vetting harness that evaluates compact quantized variants (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) prior to publishing a performance profile and pin. The harness should combine functional accuracy checks, SLO-aware latency sampling (including tail latency), memory/peak GPU footprint measurement, and lightweight model-quality tests on representative prompt families. The outcome is a binary publish decision (accept/reject) plus a structured perf profile artifact that can be consumed by the model registry and rollout system.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs end-to-end on a new quant artifact and emits a structured perf profile JSON that includes latency distribution, memory footprint, token throughput, and pass/fail quality gates.
Latency tail guard: p99 increase vs float baseline must be <= 35% for latency-sensitive routes, otherwise variant is flagged for manual review.

Quality regression guard: top-line evaluation (subset of standard prompt families) must show no >1.5% absolute drop in key metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/QA accuracy depending on model family) or the variant is rejected.
Canary sample config generated and stored alongside the profile: sample size, traffic ramp plan, rollback thresholds.
Artifacts are signed and stored in the quant artifact registry with a manifest that includes model hash, quant config, benchmark commit id, and canary policy.
Telemetry plumbing: new regression signal metrics are emitted to the runtime dashboard and can be used by the regression alerting pipeline (alert runbook stub included).
tasks: Design perf profile schema and add fields for compact variants (quant_type, scale_tables_hash, kernel_hint, stat_summary)
Implement harness runner that schedules artifact through microbench, eval subset, and memory probe (GPU peak measurement)
Integrate telemetry emitters for p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec, and per-prompt quality deltas
Create canary policy generator that produces ramp/rollback thresholds and sample sizes based on inferred SLO sensitivity
Wire publish step to model registry with artifact signing and manifest upload
End-to-end tests: synthetic load + smoke accuracy checks in CI, snapshot of perf profile stored as test artifact
canary_plan: Stage 0: internal smoke with 0.5% of traffic, sample size = 500 requests across prompt families
Stage 1: 2% traffic for 1 hour, sample size target = 2k requests, check p95/p99 and quality delta
Stage 2: 10% traffic for 3 hours, check sustained throughput and memory behavior
Rollback triggers: any p99 increase >50% vs baseline, quality delta >2.5% absolute, or OOM events in 5m window
Rollforward: automated when metrics are stable for 6 hours with error rates < baseline + 0.2%
artifact_format: Artifact manifest must be a signed JSON with: artifact_id, base_model_hash, quant_type, quant_config_blob_ref, kernel_hints, perf_profile_ref, created_by, benchmark_commit, checksum
